title: Minimal permutation-invariant qubit code for two errors
original_statement: Determine whether n_min^PI(2) = 19, where n_min^PI(2) = min{n >= 1 : there exists a complex two-dimensional subspace Q of Sym^n(C^2) with distance d(Q) >= 5}. Sym^n(C^2) consists of n-qubit vectors fixed by every qubit permutation. In an orthonormal logical basis, write |a_L> = sum_{w=0}^n c_{a,w}|D_w^n>, a in {0,1}, with unrestricted complex coefficients and |D_w^n> = binom(n,w)^(-1/2) sum_{x in {0,1}^n, |x|=w}|x>. Require sum_w conjugate(c_{a,w})c_{b,w} = delta_ab and <a_L|E|b_L> = lambda_E delta_ab for every n-qubit Pauli tensor E of weight at most 4, with lambda_E independent of a,b. These conditions correct arbitrary errors supported on at most two qubits. Use the published nineteen-qubit existence result as the literature baseline, checking its certificate before relying on it. Establish minimality by excluding every shorter length, or disprove it with a rigorously certified shorter code.

quantifiers: All candidate two-dimensional complex subspaces of Sym^n(C^2); a lower bound must cover n = 1,...,18.
All normalized orthogonal logical bases and complex Dicke amplitudes, including zeros and degenerate cases.
All locations and operators for errors on at most two qubits; equivalently detect every Pauli tensor of weight 0 through 4.
Both even and odd block lengths.
dimensions: Physical local dimension 2; total n-qubit Hilbert-space dimension 2^n.
Symmetric-subspace dimension n+1; logical dimension exactly 2; target distance at least 5.
allowed_resources: Any subspace code within the symmetric sector; recovery operations are unrestricted.
Analytic arguments, exact algebra, rigorously bounded computations, and formal verification.
Numerical optimization may find candidates; feasibility and global exclusion require justified certificates.
A restricted family may be studied as partial progress, with its gap to unrestricted codes stated explicitly.
conventions: Permutation invariance is pointwise invariance of every code vector.
Dicke states are normalized; w counts ones in the computational basis.
Distance five corresponds to two arbitrary correctable errors, not five correctable errors.
Pauli weight counts nonidentity tensor factors. The compression scalar may depend on E, but not on logical indices.
Gauge fixing, real amplitudes, support patterns, or codeword symmetries require a proof of completeness before supporting a universal lower bound.

original_scope: Prove nonexistence for every n < 19 without an unproved restriction, and establish or verify the n=19 existence baseline.
Alternatively, give a shorter symmetric two-dimensional code with a complete exact or rigorously bounded verification of every required error condition.
restricted_scope: A new certified excluded length, stronger universal bound, validated reduction, or obstruction for a stated family may be retained as partial progress.
Name the remaining lengths, coefficient classes, or missing completeness argument.
insufficient_evidence: Repeating a known nineteen-qubit construction does not by itself establish minimality.
Failed local optimization, equation counting, small residuals, and exhaustive-looking finite sampling do not by themselves prove nonexistence.
A result for real coefficients or a parity/mirror ansatz requires an additional argument to cover unrestricted complex codes and both length parities.

suggested_first_steps: Reconstruct the symmetric-sector error-compression equations and justify that the selected operator basis covers all required Pauli errors.
Check the published upper-bound certificate and the applicability of the quantum Singleton bound; its distance-five specialization rules out n <= 8.
Investigate intrinsic MacWilliams bounds for K=2 and distance five at n=9,...,18; retain exact dual certificates for any exclusion and identify cases where the relaxation is inconclusive.
Use restricted polynomial families only as explicit subproblems unless their coverage of all codes is proved.
